title.zh: 卷一百〇九 漢書11: 列傳六 杜重威 李守貞 趙思綰
title.en: Volume 109 Book of Later Jin 11: Biographies 6 - Du Zhongwei, Li Shouzhen, Zhao Siwan
title.raw: 卷一百〇九 漢書11: 列傳六 杜重威 李守貞 趙思綰 Volume 109 Book of Later Jin 11: Biographies 6 - Du Zhongwei, Li Shouzhen, Zhao Siwan

sentences.zh: 杜重威，其先朔州人，近世徙家於太原。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei: his ancestors were people of Shuozhou; in recent generations the family moved to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei came from Shuozhou stock; in recent generations his family had settled in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖興，振武牙將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xing was a Zhenwu militia officer.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xing had served as a militia officer at Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 父堆金，事唐武皇為先鋒使。

translations.literal: His father Duijin served Tang's Martial Emperor as vanguard commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duijin had served Li Keyong as commissioner of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 重威少事明宗，自護聖軍校領防州刺史。

translations.literal: In his youth Chongwei served Emperor Mingzong; he rose from an officer of the Imperial Guard corps to hold the post of prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he entered the service of Emperor Mingzong, rising from a company officer in the Imperial Guard to the prefecture of Fang.

sentences.zh: 其妻即晉高祖妹也，累封宋國大長公主。

translations.literal: His wife was the younger sister of Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin; she was repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Princess of the Song state.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a younger sister of the Later Jin founder; she was eventually enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Song.

sentences.zh: 天福初，命重威典禁軍，遙授舒州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, Chongwei was ordered to command the forbidden army and was given the nominal post of prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianfu reign he was placed in command of the palace guard and given the honorary title of prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 二年，張從賓構亂，據汜水，晉高祖遣重威與候益率眾破之，以功授潞州節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year, Zhang Congbin raised a rebellion and held the Meng ford; Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent Chongwei with Hou Yi to lead troops and defeat him; for merit he was made military commissioner of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Zhang Congbin rebelled and held the Meng crossing, the Jin founder sent Chongwei with Hou Yi to crush him; for this he was made military commissioner of Lu.

sentences.zh: 與楊光遠降範延光於鄴城，改許州節度使，兼侍衛親軍馬步軍副指揮使，尋加同平章事。

translations.literal: With Yang Guangyuan he induced Fan Yanguang to surrender at Yecheng; he was made military commissioner of Xu Prefecture, concurrently deputy commander of the palace cavalry and infantry, and soon after was added as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yang Guangyuan induced Fan Yanguang to surrender at Ye; he was then made military commissioner of Xu, deputy commander of the palace armies, and soon after also co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移鎮鄆州，遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to govern Yan Prefecture and was promoted to commander of the palace cavalry and infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was shifted to Yan Prefecture and advanced to full commander of the palace cavalry and infantry.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：馮道、李崧屢薦重威之能，以為都指揮使，充隨駕御營使。）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly recommended Chongwei's ability, appointing him commander-in-chief and assigning him as attendant commander of the imperial escort camp.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Comprehensive Mirror records: Feng Dao and Li Song repeatedly commended Chongwei's ability, securing his appointment as commander-in-chief and assigning him to oversee the emperor's accompanying camp.)〉

sentences.zh: 及鎮州安重榮稱兵向闕，命重威禦之，敗重榮於宗城。

translations.literal: When An Chongrong of Zhen Prefecture raised troops and marched toward the capital, Chongwei was ordered to resist him and defeated Chongrong at Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When An Chongrong of Zhenzhou raised an army and marched on the capital, Chongwei was ordered against him and defeated him at Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 重榮奔據常山，重威尋拔其城，斬重榮首傳於闕下，授成德軍節度使。

translations.literal: Chongrong fled and held Changshan; Chongwei soon captured the city, beheaded Chongrong, and sent his head to below the palace gates; he was made military commissioner of the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong fled to Changshan, which Chongwei soon took; he beheaded Chongrong and sent his head to the capital, receiving appointment as military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 所得重榮家財及常山公帑，悉歸於己，晉高祖知而不問。

translations.literal: The property of Chongrong's household and the public funds of Changshan he took entirely for himself; Emperor Gaozu of Jin knew but did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: He appropriated all of Chongrong's household property and the Changshan treasury for himself; the Jin founder knew yet asked nothing.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，復重斂於民，稅外加賦，境內苦之

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post, he again taxed the people heavily, imposing levies beyond the regular taxes, and the territory suffered bitterly
translations.idiomatic: Once in his command, he taxed the people again with heavy exactions beyond the regular levies, and the region groaned under it

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：重威所至黷貨，民多逃亡，嘗出過市，謂左右曰：「人言我驅盡百姓，何市人之多也！」）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Wherever Chongwei went he rapaciously seized goods; the people fled in great numbers. Once when he went out and passed through the market he said to his attendants, "People say I have driven away all the common people—why are there so many in the market!")〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Comprehensive Mirror states: Wherever Chongwei served he plundered, and the people fled in droves. Once, passing through the marketplace, he said to his attendants, "They say I have driven out every commoner—then why are there so many people in the market!")〉

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，與契丹絕好，契丹主連年伐晉，重威但閉壁自守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded, relations with the Khitan were broken; the Khitan ruler invaded Jin year after year; Chongwei only closed his walls and defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the Young Emperor succeeded, the court broke with the Khitan; the Khitan khan invaded Jin year upon year, while Chongwei only shut himself behind his walls.

sentences.zh: 部內城邑相繼破陷，一境生靈受屠戮，重威任居方面，未嘗以一土一騎救之。

translations.literal: Cities and towns within his jurisdiction were successively captured; the living things of the whole region suffered slaughter; though Chongwei held a frontier command, he never sent a single foot of earth or a single horse to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Town after town in his command fell; the people of the whole region were butchered, yet though he held a frontier post he never sent a single soldier or patch of territory to their relief.

sentences.zh: 每敵騎數十驅漢人千萬過城下，如入無人之境，重威但登陴註目，略無邀取之意。

translations.literal: Each time several tens of enemy horsemen would drive millions of Han people past below the city walls, as if entering territory where there were no men; Chongwei would only ascend the battlements and watch, with virtually no intention of intercepting them.
translations.idiomatic: Often a few dozen enemy horsemen would drive millions of Han subjects past the walls, as through empty land; Chongwei would only climb the ramparts and watch, scarcely meaning to strike at them.

sentences.zh: 開運元年秋，加北面行營招討使。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Kaiyun he was added as northern-line commander and superintendent of punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first Kaiyun year he was made commander of the northern expeditionary force.

sentences.zh: 二年，領大軍下新州、滿城、遂城。

translations.literal: In the second year he led the great army down through Xin, Mancheng, and Suicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he led the main army against Xin, Mancheng, and Suicheng.

sentences.zh: 契丹主自古北口回軍，追躡王師，重威等狼狽而旋，至陽城，為契丹所困。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler returned his army from Guyuan Pass and pursued the imperial army; Chongwei and the others turned back in distress; at Yangcheng they were beset by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan marched back from Guyuan and pursued the imperial force; Chongwei's column fell back in disorder and at Yangcheng was trapped by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 會大風狂猛，軍情憤激，府彥卿、張彥澤等引軍四出，敵眾大潰，諸將欲追之，重威曰：「逢賊得命，更望復子乎！

translations.literal: When a violent gale arose the army's spirit was inflamed; Fu Yanqing, Zhang Yanze, and others led troops out on all sides and the enemy forces were utterly routed; the generals wished to pursue them; Chongwei said, "Having met the foe and kept our lives, do we still hope to have children again!
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind sprang up and the troops' anger boiled over; Fu Yanqing, Zhang Yanze, and others led sorties on every side and the enemy broke completely. When the generals wanted to pursue, Chongwei said, "We met the enemy and barely kept our lives—do we still expect to see our children again?

sentences.zh: 」遂收軍馳歸常山。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gathered the army and galloped back to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: " He then drew off the army and rode back to Changshan.

sentences.zh: 先是，重威於州內括借錢帛，吏民大被其苦，人情鹹怨，重以境內雕弊，十室九空，重威遂無留意，連上表乞歸朝，不俟報即時上路。

translations.literal: Earlier, within the prefecture Chongwei had requisitioned money and silk by force; officials and people suffered terribly; sentiment was unanimous in resentment; again, as the territory within was devastated and nine of ten houses stood empty, Chongwei lost all interest, repeatedly submitted memorials begging to return to court, and set out on the road at once without awaiting a reply.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier forced loans of money and cloth from the prefecture, to the people's great suffering, and resentment ran deep. With the land inside his borders wasted and nine houses in ten empty, he lost heart, sent memorial after memorial asking leave to return to court, and took the road without waiting for a reply.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以邊上重鎮，主帥擅離，茍有奔沖，慮失禦備，然亦無如之何，即以馬全節代之，重威尋授鄴都留守。

translations.literal: The court regarded this as a weighty frontier post whose commander had left on his own authority; if there were a sudden raid they feared loss of defense—but there was nothing to be done; Ma Quanjie was immediately sent to replace him; Chongwei soon received appointment as defender of the Yedu capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court saw a critical frontier whose commander had quit on his own; any sudden thrust might leave them undefended, yet they could do nothing. Ma Quanjie replaced him at once, while Chongwei was soon named defender of Yedu.

sentences.zh: 會鎮州軍食不繼，遣殿中監王欽祚就本州和市，重威私第有粟十餘萬斛，遂錄之以聞。

translations.literal: When Zhen Prefecture's army provisions would not hold out, the palace supervisor Wang Qinzuo was sent to that prefecture to purchase grain in the market; at Chongwei's private residence there were more than one hundred thousand piculs of grain, and it was inventoried and reported.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhou ran short of rations, the palace supervisor Wang Qinzuo was sent to buy grain there; more than one hundred thousand piculs were found in Chongwei's private store and reported to court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷給絹數萬匹，償其粟直。

translations.literal: The court gave several tens of thousands of bolts of silk to compensate the value of the grain.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid him several ten thousands of bolts of silk as the grain's price.

sentences.zh: 重威大忿曰：「我非反逆，安得籍沒耶！

translations.literal: Chongwei was greatly angered and said, "Am I not a rebel—why should my property be confiscated!
translations.idiomatic: Furious, he cried, "I am no rebel—why treat me like a confiscation case!

sentences.zh: 」三年冬，晉少帝詔重威與李守貞等率師經略瀛、鄚。

translations.literal: " In the winter of the third year, Emperor Shaodi of Jin ordered Chongwei with Li Shouzhen and others to lead troops to take the field in Ying and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: " In the winter of the third year the Young Emperor ordered Chongwei and Li Shouzhen east against Ying and Mo.

sentences.zh: 師至瀛州城下，晉騎將梁漢璋與契丹接戰，漢璋死焉。

translations.literal: When the army reached below the walls of Ying Prefecture, the Jin cavalry general Liang Hanzhang engaged the Khitan in battle and Hanzhang died.
translations.idiomatic: Below the walls of Yingzhou the Jin cavalry commander Liang Hanzhang met the Khitan in battle and was killed.

sentences.zh: 重威即時回軍，次武強，聞契丹主南下，乃西趨鎮州，至中渡橋，與契丹夾滹水而營。

translations.literal: Chongwei immediately turned the army back and halted at Wuqiang; hearing the Khitan ruler was marching south, he hurried west toward Zhen Prefecture; at the Zhongdu ford bridge he camped on the Hutuo River facing the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei withdrew at once and encamped at Wuqiang; hearing the Khitan khan was moving south, he hurried to Zhenzhou and at Zhongdu Bridge pitched camp across the Hutuo from the enemy.

sentences.zh: 十二月八日，宋彥筠、王清等率數千人渡滹沲，陣於北岸，為敵所破。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the twelfth month, Song Yanzhi, Wang Qing, and others led several thousand men across the Hutuo River and formed battle lines on the north bank; they were broken by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth of the twelfth month Song Yanzhi and Wang Qing led a few thousand men across the river and formed on the north bank; the enemy shattered them.

sentences.zh: 時契丹遊軍已至欒城，道路隔絕，人情危蹙，重威密遣人詣敵帳，潛布腹心。

translations.literal: At that time Khitan patrols had already reached Luancheng; roads were cut off; feeling was tense; Chongwei secretly sent men to the enemy camp and quietly placed trusted agents.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan scouts had already reached Luancheng, the roads were cut, and morale was desperate. Chongwei secretly sent envoys to the enemy camp and planted intimates there.

sentences.zh: 契丹主大悅，許以中原帝之，重威庸暗，深以為信。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased and promised him the throne of Central Plains; Chongwei was dull and obtuse and deeply believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan was delighted and promised him the Central Plains throne; dull and credulous, Chongwei believed it completely.

sentences.zh: 一日，伏甲於內，召諸將會，告以降敵之意，諸將愕然。

translations.literal: One day he set armed men in hiding within and summoned the generals to a meeting, announcing his intention to surrender to the enemy; the generals were stunned.
translations.idiomatic: One day he hid armed men inside, summoned the generals, and declared he would surrender; they were stunned.

sentences.zh: 以上將既變，乃俯首聽命，遂連署降表，令中門使高勛賫送敵帳，軍士解甲，舉聲慟哭。

translations.literal: Since the supreme commander had already changed his mind, they could only bow their heads and heed orders; they then jointly signed a surrender memorial, ordered the inner gate commissioner Gao Xun to carry it to the enemy camp, the soldiers doffed their armor, and a sound of wailing arose.
translations.idiomatic: With their commander already decided, they had no choice but to obey. They signed a joint surrender, sent the inner-gate commissioner Gao Xun with it to the enemy camp, the troops stripped their armor, and a great wailing broke out.

sentences.zh: 是日，有大霧起於降軍之上。

translations.literal: That day, heavy fog rose above the surrendered army.
translations.idiomatic: That day a great fog rose over the surrendered host.

sentences.zh: 契丹主使重威衣赭袍以示諸軍，尋偽加守太傅，鄴都留守如故。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler made Chongwei wear an ochre-red robe to show the armies; he was soon falsely advanced as Grand Tutor while remaining defender of Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan had him dress in ochre robes to display before the armies; he was soon given the false title Grand Tutor while keeping Yedu.

sentences.zh: 契丹主南行，命重威部轄晉軍以從，既至東京，駐晉軍於陳橋，士伍饑凍，不勝其苦。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler marched south and ordered Chongwei to command the Jin armies to follow; when they reached the Eastern Capital they encamped the Jin forces at Chenqiao; soldiers suffered hunger and cold beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The khan marched south and put the Jin troops under Chongwei; at the Eastern Capital they were held at Chenqiao, starving and freezing past endurance.

sentences.zh: 重威每出入衢路，為市民所詬，俯首而已。

translations.literal: Each time Chongwei went out on the thoroughfares he was cursed by citizens of the market; he only bowed his head.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he passed through the streets townspeople cursed him; he only lowered his head.

sentences.zh: 契丹下令括率京城錢帛，將相公私，雷同率配，重威與李守貞各萬緡，乃告契丹主曰：「臣等以十萬漢軍降於皇帝，不免配借，臣所不甘。

translations.literal: The Khitan issued orders to levy money and silk throughout the capital; among ministers and commanders, public and private, all were assessed alike; Chongwei and Li Shouzhen each owed ten thousand strings; they then told the Khitan ruler, "We brought one hundred thousand Han troops to surrender to Your Majesty, yet still are not spared forced levies—this we cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ordered a levy on the capital's wealth from ministers down, public and private alike; Chongwei and Li Shouzhen each owed ten thousand strings. They pleaded, "We led a hundred thousand Han troops to surrender to Your Majesty, yet are still forced to pay—this we cannot stomach.

sentences.zh: 」契丹主笑而免之。

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler laughed and exempted them.
translations.idiomatic: " The khan laughed and let them off.

sentences.zh: 尋群盜斷澶州浮梁，契丹乃遣重威歸藩。

translations.literal: Before long bandits cut the floating bridge at Cang Prefecture; the Khitan then sent Chongwei back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels severed the Cangzhou pontoon bridge; the Khitan then sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，契丹主北去，至相州城下，重威與妻石氏詣牙帳貢獻而回。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year the Khitan ruler went north; reaching below the walls of Xiang Prefecture, Chongwei with his wife Lady Shi went to the military tent to offer tribute and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the third month, the khan marched north; at Xiangzhou Chongwei and his wife Lady Shi came to the tent with tribute and returned.

sentences.zh: 高祖車駕至闕，以重威為宋州節度使，加守太尉。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor's imperial carriage reached the palace gates, Chongwei was made military commissioner of Song Prefecture and added as Defender Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhiyuan's procession reached the capital, Chongwei was named military commissioner of Song and honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 重威懼，閉城拒命，詔高行周率兵攻討，重威遣其子宏遂等告急於鎮州州麻答，乞師救援，旦以宏遂為質，麻答遣蕃將楊兗赴之。

translations.literal: Chongwei was afraid, shut the city gates and refused orders; an edict ordered Gao Xingzhou to lead troops to attack; Chongwei sent his son Hongsui and others to urge Ma Da of Zhen Prefecture to send relief; each morning he gave Hongsui as hostage; Ma Da sent the tribal general Yang Yan to go.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, he shut the gates and defied the court. Gao Xingzhou was ordered against him; Chongwei sent his son Hongsui to Ma Da at Zhenzhou begging troops, offering the boy as hostage each dawn; Ma Da sent the tribal officer Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鎮州軍逐滿達勒，楊兗至洺州而回。

translations.literal: Before long the army of Zhen Prefecture drove out Mandale; Yang Yan reached Luozhou and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhenzhou's garrison expelled Mandale, and Yang Yan reached Luozhou only to turn back.

sentences.zh: 十月，高祖親征，車駕至鄴城之下，遣給事中陳觀等賫詔入城，許其歸命，重威不納。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the High Ancestor personally campaigned; when the imperial carriage reached below Yecheng he sent the edict attendant Chen Guan and others bearing an edict into the city, promising that if he submitted his life would be spared; Chongwei would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Liu Zhiyuan campaigned in person; below Ye he sent Chen Guan with an edict into the city offering mercy if he surrendered; Chongwei refused.

sentences.zh: 數日，高祖親率諸軍攻其壘，不克，王師傷夷者萬餘人。

translations.literal: After several days the High Ancestor personally led the armies to attack his ramparts but could not take them; the imperial army had more than ten thousand wounded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the emperor led the assault but failed; imperial casualties ran above ten thousand.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·杜漢徽傳》云：從高行周討杜重威於鄴城，屢為流矢所中，身被重創，猶力戰，觀者壯之。）〉

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Du Hanhui: Following Gao Xingzhou in attacking Du Chongwei at Yecheng, he was repeatedly struck by stray arrows, received severe wounds over his body, yet still fought fiercely; onlookers admired his valor.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Song, Biography of Du Hanhui: In the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye under Gao Xingzhou he was hit again and again by stray arrows and bore heavy wounds all over, yet kept fighting; observers were stirred by his courage.)〉

sentences.zh: 高祖駐軍數旬，城中糧盡，屑麹餅以給軍士，吏民逾壘而出者甚眾，皆無人色。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor encamped the army for several tens of days; within the city grain was exhausted and they fed the soldiers with bran cakes; officials and people climbing over the ramparts to flee were very numerous, all without color in their faces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor camped there for weeks; inside, grain ran out and the garrison ate bran cakes; multitudes climbed out over the walls to escape, faces bloodless.

sentences.zh: 至是，重威牙將詣行宮請降，復遣節度判官王敏奉表請罪，賜優詔敦勉，許其如初。

translations.literal: At this point Chongwei's commanders came to the forward camp to request surrender; he again sent the administrative aide Wang Min with a memorial begging forgiveness; an excellent edict was bestowed warmly encouraging him, promising conditions as before.
translations.idiomatic: Then his staff officers came to the emperor's camp to sue for surrender; Wang Min followed with a memorial of repentance; a generous edict reassured him that terms would stand as before.

sentences.zh: 重威即遣其子宏遂、妻石氏出候高祖，重威繼踵出降，素服俟罪，復其衣冠，賜見，即日制授檢校太師、守太傅、兼中書令。

translations.literal: Chongwei immediately sent his son Hongsui and wife Lady Shi out to await the High Ancestor; Chongwei followed close behind in surrender, in plain dress awaiting punishment; his normal robes were restored; an audience was granted; that very day an edict appointed him Grand Master, Defender Grand Tutor, and Chancellor of the Secretariat concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hongsui and Lady Shi ahead to meet the emperor, then came out himself in mourning dress to await judgment; his robes were restored, he was received in audience, and that day was made Grand Master, honorary Grand Tutor, and Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 鄴城士庶，殍殕者十之六七。

translations.literal: Of the people of Yecheng, six or seven in ten perished.
translations.idiomatic: Of Ye's townspeople, six or seven in ten died.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹遣幽州指揮使張璉，以部下軍二千餘人屯鄴，時亦有燕軍一千五百人在京師，會高祖至闕，有上變者，言燕軍謀亂，盡誅於繁臺之下，咸稱其冤。

translations.literal: Earlier the Khitan had sent Zhang Lian of Youzhou as garrison commander with a little more than two thousand troops below the city; at that time there were also fifteen hundred Yan troops in the capital; when the High Ancestor reached the palace gates someone reported a plot by the Yan troops; they were all executed below Fantai; all said they were wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan had left Zhang Lian of Youzhou with just over two thousand men in Ye, while fifteen hundred Yan troops were also in the capital. When Liu Zhiyuan arrived, a report claimed the Yan soldiers meant revolt; all were killed below Fantai, and many called it a wrongful slaughter.

sentences.zh: 有逃奔於鄴者，備言其事，故張璉等懼死，與重威膠固守城，略無叛誌。

translations.literal: Some fled to Ye and explained everything in detail; therefore Zhang Lian and the others feared death and with Chongwei clung grimly to the city, with virtually no thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Escapees reached Ye with full accounts, so Zhang Lian and the rest, fearing execution, held the city grimly with Chongwei, with no real intent to rebel.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦悔其前失，累令宣諭，許以不死。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor also regretted his earlier mistake and repeatedly sent proclamations reassuring them, promising they would not die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor too regretted his earlier act and repeatedly proclaimed they would not be put to death.

sentences.zh: 璉等於城上揚言曰：「繁臺之誅，燕軍何罪？

translations.literal: Zhang Lian and the others shouted from atop the wall, "At the Fantai slaughter, what crime did the Yan troops commit?
translations.idiomatic: From the wall Zhang Lian called out, "At Fantai, what crime did the Yan soldiers commit?

sentences.zh: 既無生理，以死為期。

translations.literal: Having no way to live, we take death as our term.
translations.idiomatic: Given no way to live, we look only to die fighting."

sentences.zh: 」璉一軍在圍中，重威推食解衣，盡力姑息。

translations.literal: " Zhang Lian's one army was within the siege; Chongwei shared his food and stripped off his clothes, doing his utmost to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lian's force was trapped in the siege; Chongwei shared his rations and gave them his own clothes, indulging them to the limit.

sentences.zh: 燕軍驕悍，憑陵吏民，子女金帛，公行豪奪。

translations.literal: The Yan troops were arrogant and ferocious, riding roughshod over officials and people; daughters, gold, and silk they openly seized by force.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan soldiers were brutal and overbearing; they openly seized people's daughters, gold, and goods.

sentences.zh: 及重威請命，璉等邀朝廷信誓，詔許璉等卻歸本土。

translations.literal: When Chongwei asked to surrender, Zhang Lian and the others demanded written assurances from the court; an edict promised Zhang Lian and the others could return to their native land.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongwei sought to capitulate, Zhang Lian demanded sworn guarantees; an edict promised the Yan troops safe return home.

sentences.zh: 及出降，盡誅璉等將數十人，其什長已下放歸幽州，將出漢境，剽略而去。

translations.literal: When they came out in surrender, several tens of commanders including Zhang Lian were all executed; the squad leaders had already been sent down to Youzhou; as they were about to leave Han territory they plundered along the way.
translations.idiomatic: After the surrender dozens of officers including Zhang Lian were executed; lower ranks had already been sent toward Youzhou; just before leaving Han territory they looted the countryside on their way out.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣三司使王章、樞密副使郭威，錄重威部下將吏盡誅之，籍其財產與重威私帑，分給將士。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor sent the Three Bureaus Commissioner Wang Zhang and Vice Director of the Secretariat Guo Wei to record and execute all of Chongwei's subordinate officers and generals, register their property together with Chongwei's private stores, and distribute it to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Zhang of the Three Bureaus and Guo Wei, vice director of the Secretariat, to register and execute all of Chongwei's officers, seize their property with his private hoard, and distribute it among the troops.

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，高祖不豫，既而大漸。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, the High Ancestor was unwell and soon fell into grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to the palace the emperor fell ill and soon grew desperately sick.

sentences.zh: 顧命之際，謂近臣將佐曰：「善防重威。

translations.literal: At the moment of final instructions he said to his close ministers and assistants, "Take good care to guard against Chongwei.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his close advisers, "Guard against Chongwei carefully.

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，遂收重威，重威子宏璋、宏璉、宏傑誅之。

translations.literal: " When the emperor died, Chongwei was immediately arrested; Chongwei's sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongjie were executed.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor died Chongwei was seized at once, with his sons Hongzhang, Honglian, and Hongjie.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「杜重威猶貯禍心，未悛逆節，梟音不改，虺性難馴。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Du Chongwei still harbors a treacherous heart and has not reformed his rebellious conduct; his owl cry remains unchanged and his viper nature is hard to tame.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Du Chongwei still nurses treason and has not mended his rebellion; his nature remains vicious and his malice intractable.

sentences.zh: 昨朕小有不安，罷朝數日，而重威父子潛肆兇言，怨謗大朝，扇惑小輩；

translations.literal: Yesterday when I had a slight indisposition and suspended court for several days, Chongwei father and son secretly uttered fierce words, slandering the great court and inciting petty men;
translations.idiomatic: When I fell briefly ill and missed court for several days, father and son secretly spoke violent words, reviling the dynasty and stirring up petty followers;

sentences.zh: 今則顯有陳告，備驗奸期。

translations.literal: now there are explicit denunciations and the wicked plot is fully verified.
translations.idiomatic: now clear reports have come in and their treachery is fully proved.

sentences.zh: 既負深恩，須置極法，其杜重威父子並處斬。

translations.literal: Having betrayed deep grace, they must be placed under the extreme penalty; Du Chongwei father and son are all to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Having betrayed profound favor, they merit the harshest punishment: father and son shall be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 所有晉朝公主及外親族，一切如常，仍與供給。

translations.literal: All princesses of the Jin court and all collateral kin are to remain as before, with provisions continued.
translations.idiomatic: All Later Jin princesses and affinal kin are to be treated as before, with support continued.

sentences.zh: 」重威父子已誅，陳屍於通衢，都人聚觀者詬罵蹴擊，軍吏不能禁，屍首狼籍，斯須而盡。

translations.literal: " After Chongwei father and son were executed their corpses were displayed on the main thoroughfare; the people of the capital gathered to curse, kick, and strike them; military officers could not restrain them; the corpses were strewn in disorder and in an instant were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were dead their bodies were left on the highway; crowds cursed them, kicked them, and tore them apart beyond the guards' control until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 宏璉，重威之子也，累官至陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Honglian, son of Chongwei, rose through offices to prefect of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Honglian, another of Chongwei's sons, had risen to prefect of Chen.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》：黨進，幼為天雄軍節度使杜重威奴，重威愛其淳謹，雖長，猶令與婢妾雜侍。

translations.literal: (Longping Records: Dang Jin, in youth a slave of Tianxiong military commissioner Du Chongwei; Chongwei loved his honest carefulness and though he grew to manhood still had him wait among the maids and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: (The Longping Records state: Dang Jin had been a boy slave to Du Chongwei, military commissioner of Tianxiong; Chongwei prized his plain dutifulness and, though he grew up, still kept him among the serving women.

sentences.zh: 重威敗，周祖得之，以為鐵騎都虞候。

translations.literal: When Chongwei was defeated, Emperor Taizu of Zhou obtained him and made him chief officer of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongwei's fall, the Zhou founder took him in and made him chief registrar of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 重威之後寒餓，進常分俸以給，士大夫或愧焉。）〉

translations.literal: After Chongwei's line fell into cold hunger, Jin regularly shared his salary to support them; some literati felt ashamed of this.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When Chongwei's family fell into poverty, Jin often divided his pay to help them—an act some gentlemen found embarrassing.)〉

sentences.zh: 李守貞，河陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen, a man of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen came from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 少桀黠落魄，事本部為牙將。

translations.literal: In youth he was brutal, crafty, and down on his luck; he served his district as a militia officer.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was unruly, sharp-witted, and destitute; he served his circuit as a militia officer.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖鎮河陽，用為典客，後移數鎮，皆從之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Jin governed Heyang he used him as protocol attendant; afterward when he moved through several commands Shouzhen followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder governed Heyang he used him on ceremonial duty, and Shouzhen followed him through each subsequent command.

sentences.zh: 及即位，累遷至客省使。

translations.literal: When he took the throne Shouzhen was repeatedly promoted up to Commissioner of the Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession Shouzhen rose step by step to Commissioner of the Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天福中，李金全以安州叛，淮夷入寇，晉高祖命馬全節討之，守貞監護其軍，賊平，守貞為宣徽使。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu period, Li Jinquan rebelled with An Prefecture; the Huai tribes invaded; Emperor Gaozu of Jin ordered Ma Quanjie to subdue them; Shouzhen supervised the army; when the bandits were pacified Shouzhen became Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, when Li Jinquan rebelled at Anzhou and Huai enemies raided in, the founder sent Ma Quanjie to suppress them with Shouzhen overseeing the campaign; after victory he became Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，授滑州節度兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使，未幾，改侍衛都虞候。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi succeeded he was made military commissioner of Hua Prefecture concurrently with commander of the palace cavalry; before long he was changed to chief commander of the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Young Emperor he became commissioner of Hua and commander of the palace cavalry, then soon chief commander of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 開運元年春，敵眾犯澶、魏，少帝幸澶州，契丹遣將麻答以奇兵由鄆州馬家口濟河，立柵於東岸，守貞率師自澶州馳赴之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Kaiyun the enemy masses invaded Cang and Wei; the Young Emperor went to Cang Prefecture; the Khitan sent the general Ma Da with elite troops crossing the Yellow River at the Ma family ford of Yan Prefecture, establishing a stockade on the east bank; Shouzhen led troops from Cang Prefecture to rush there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Kaiyun spring the enemy struck Cang and Wei; the Young Emperor went to Cangzhou; the Khitan general Ma Da crossed at Yanzhou's Ma family ford with picked troops and entrenched on the east bank; Shouzhen raced from Cangzhou to meet him.

sentences.zh: 契丹大敗，溺死者數千人，獲馬數百匹，偏裨七十餘人。

translations.literal: The Khitan suffered a great defeat; several thousand drowned; several hundred horses were captured; more than seventy commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were routed; thousands drowned; hundreds of horses and more than seventy officers were taken.

sentences.zh: 有頃，敵退。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝還京，以守貞為兗州節度使，依前侍衛都虞候。

translations.literal: Emperor Shaodi of Jin returned to the capital and made Shouzhen military commissioner of Yan Prefecture, remaining as before chief commander of the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor returned to the capital, made him commissioner of Yan, and kept him as chief palace guard commander.

sentences.zh: 五月，以守貞為青州行營都部署，率兵二萬東討楊光遠，命符彥卿為副。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was made eastern-line chief commander, leading twenty thousand troops east to attack Yang Guangyuan; Fu Yanqing was appointed deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was named eastern expedition commander with twenty thousand men against Yang Guangyuan, with Fu Yanqing as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 十一月，光遠子承勛等乞降，守貞入城，害光遠於別第。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Guangyuan's son Chengxun and others begged to surrender; Shouzhen entered the city and killed Guangyuan in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Chengxun asked to surrender; Shouzhen entered the city and killed Guangyuan in his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 光遠有孔目官吏宋顏者，盡以光遠財寶、名姬、善馬告於守貞，得之置於帳下。

translations.literal: Guangyuan had a clerical officer Song Yan who reported all of Guangyuan's treasure, famous concubines, and fine horses to Shouzhen; having obtained them he placed them in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk named Song Yan revealed all of Guangyuan's wealth, noted concubines, and best horses; Shouzhen took them into his own camp.

sentences.zh: 近例，官軍克復城隍，必降德音，洗滌瑕穢，時樞密使桑維翰以光遠同惡數十輩潛竄未出，搜索甚急，故制書久不下。

translations.literal: By recent precedent when government troops recovered a walled city a mercy edict was always issued to wash away faults; at that time Secretariat Director Sang Weihan, because several dozen of Guangyuan's accomplices were still hiding and the search was very urgent, the decree was long in coming down.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, recapture of a city brought an amnesty to clear petty guilt; but Sang Weihan at the Secretariat kept the edict back while dozens of Guangyuan's accomplices were hunted down.

sentences.zh: 或有告宋顏匿於守貞處者，朝廷取而殺之，守貞由是怨維翰。

translations.literal: Some reported that Song Yan was hidden at Shouzhen's place; the court took him and executed him; Shouzhen therefore resented Weihan.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Song Yan was with Shouzhen, court agents seized and killed him, and Shouzhen bore a grudge against Weihan.

sentences.zh: 時行營將士所給賞賜，守貞盡以黦茶、染木、姜藥之類分給之，軍中大怨，乃以帛包所得物，如人首級，目之為守貞頭，懸於樹以詛之。

translations.literal: At that time the rewards given to expeditionary soldiers—Shouzhen distributed to them only inferior tea, dyewood, ginger, and medicines of that sort; the army was greatly resentful and wrapped the goods in cloth like human heads, calling them "Shouzhen heads," and hung them on trees to curse him.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards came, Shouzhen handed out only cheap tea, dye-woods, ginger, and the like; the troops in fury bundled the goods like severed heads, called them "Shouzhen heads," and hung them on trees as curses.

sentences.zh: 守貞班師，加同平章事，以楊光遠東京第賜之。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen returned from campaign he was added as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery; Yang Guangyuan's Eastern Capital residence was bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made co-chancellor and given Guangyuan's mansion in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 守貞因取連宅軍營，以廣其第，大興土木，治之歲餘，為京師之甲。

translations.literal: Shouzhen then took over adjoining barracks of the combined garrison to enlarge his residence, undertaking great earthworks for more than a year, making it the finest in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He seized neighboring garrison compounds to expand the estate, built on a grand scale for more than a year, and produced the finest house in the capital.

sentences.zh: 行幸賜宴，恩禮無比。

translations.literal: On an imperial excursion a feast was bestowed; favor and ceremony were without equal.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled and feasted him, the honor shown him had no equal.

sentences.zh: 開運二年春，契丹以全軍南下，前鋒至相州湯陰縣，詔守貞屯滑州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Kaiyun the Khitan marched south with their full army; the vanguard reached Tangyin in Xiang Prefecture, and an edict ordered Shouzhen to garrison Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second Kaiyun year the Khitan came south with their whole host; their van reached Tangyin in Xiangzhou, and Shouzhen was ordered to hold Hua.

sentences.zh: 少帝再幸澶州，以守貞為北面行營都監，與招討使杜重威北伐，洎獲陽城之捷，遂收軍而還。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor again visited Cang Prefecture, Shouzhen was made superintendent of the northern expeditionary camp; together with campaign commander Du Chongwei he marched north, and after the victory at Yangcheng the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor went again to Cangzhou and named Shouzhen superintendent of the northern camp; with Du Chongwei as campaign commander they marched north, and after the victory at Yangcheng drew off the army.

sentences.zh: 四月，車駕還京，以守貞為侍衛副都指揮使，移鎮宋州，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the imperial carriage returned to the capital; Shouzhen was made deputy commander of the palace guard, transferred to govern Song Prefecture, and added as Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor returned to the capital, made him deputy commander of the palace guard, shifted him to Songzhou, and gave him the honorary title Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 三年春，詔守貞率師巡邊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year an edict ordered Shouzhen to lead troops on a border patrol.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year spring he was ordered to patrol the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至衡水，獲鄚州刺史趙思英而還。

translations.literal: At Hengshui he captured Zhao Siying, prefect of Mo Prefecture, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengshui he captured Zhao Siying, prefect of Mo, and returned.

sentences.zh: 居無何，代高行周為侍衛親軍都指揮使，移鎮鄆州，意頗觖望。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace armies and was transferred to govern Yan Prefecture; he was quite discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Gao Xingzhou as commander of the palace armies and was moved to Yanzhou, nursing considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 會宰臣李崧加侍中，守貞謂樞密使直學士殷鵬曰：「樞密何功，便加正相！

translations.literal: When Chancellor Li Song was added as Grand Mentor, Shouzhen said to the Secretariat academician Yin Peng, "What merit does the Secretariat have that it is made chief minister at once!
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Li Song was made Grand Mentor, Shouzhen told the Secretariat academician Yin Peng, "What has the Secretariat done to be made chief minister so soon!

sentences.zh: 」先是，桑維翰以元勛舊德為樞密使，守貞位望素處其下，每憚之，與李彥韜、馮玉輩協力排斥，維翰竟罷樞務。

translations.literal: " Earlier Sang Weihan, as a founding veteran, had been director of the Secretariat; Shouzhen's standing had always been below him and he feared him; working with Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and others he jointly excluded him until Weihan left Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sang Weihan, a founding veteran, had been director of the Secretariat; Shouzhen had always stood beneath him and feared him; working with Li Yantao, Feng Yu, and others he drove Weihan out of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李崧事分疏遠，守貞得以淩蔑。

translations.literal: Li Song's connection with him was distant, and Shouzhen could bully him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song was loosely connected to him, and Shouzhen treated him with contempt.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，契丹寇邊，以守貞為北面行營都部署。

translations.literal: That summer, when the Khitan raided the frontier, Shouzhen was made commander of the northern expeditionary force.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the Khitan raided the frontier, Shouzhen was made northern expedition commander.

sentences.zh: 少帝開曲宴於內殿，以寵其行，教坊令人獻語云：「天子不須憂北寇，守貞面上管幽州。

translations.literal: The Young Emperor held an informal feast in the inner hall to honor his departure; a performer from the music office offered a verse saying, "The Son of Heaven need not worry about the northern foe—Shouzhen's face governs Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Emperor gave him a private feast in the inner hall before his departure; an entertainer offered the line, "The Son of Heaven need not fear the northern foe—Shouzhen's face will hold Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 」既罷，守貞有自負之色，以其言誇詫於外。

translations.literal: " When it ended Shouzhen wore a self-satisfied look and boasted of the words outside.
translations.idiomatic: When it ended he looked pleased with himself and repeated the line abroad as boast.

sentences.zh: 既而率兵至定州北，與契丹偏師遇，斬蕃將嘉哩而還。

translations.literal: He then led troops north of Ding Prefecture, met a Khitan detachment, beheaded the tribal general Jiali, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched north of Dingzhou, met a Khitan detachment, beheaded the tribal officer Jiali, and returned.

sentences.zh: 九月，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was also added as Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was also made Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 會契丹遣瀛州刺史偽降於少帝，請發大軍應接，朝廷信之。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent the prefect of Ying Prefecture in feigned surrender to the Young Emperor, asking for a great army to meet him, and the court believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent the prefect of Ying in feigned surrender to the Young Emperor, asking for a great army to meet him, and the court believed it.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔杜重威為北面行營招討使，以守貞為兵馬都監，知幽州行府事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Du Chongwei was made northern campaign commander; Shouzhen was made cavalry superintendent and acting prefect of the Youzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Du Chongwei was named northern campaign commander, with Shouzhen as cavalry superintendent and acting prefect of the Youzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 先是，守貞領兵再由鄴都，杜重威厚加贈遺，曲意承迎，守貞悅之，每於帝前稱舉，請委征討之柄。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shouzhen again led troops through Yedu, Du Chongwei heaped gifts on him and flattered him; Shouzhen was pleased and repeatedly praised him before the emperor, asking that command of the campaign be entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shouzhen passed through Ye again with his troops, Du Chongwei heaped gifts on him and flattered him; pleased, Shouzhen praised him at court and asked that command of the campaign be entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 至是，守貞、重威等會兵於鄴，遂趨瀛州，瀛州不應。

translations.literal: At this point Shouzhen and Chongwei united their forces at Ye and hurried to Ying Prefecture, which would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shouzhen and Chongwei united at Ye and pressed on to Yingzhou, which would not answer.

sentences.zh: 貝州節度使梁漢璋為蕃將高牟翰所敗，死之，王師遂還。

translations.literal: The Bei Prefecture military commissioner Liang Hanzhang was defeated and killed by the tribal officer Gao Mouhan, and the imperial army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Bei prefect Liang Hanzhang was beaten and killed by the tribal officer Gao Mouhan, and the imperial force withdrew.

sentences.zh: 師至深州，聞契丹大至，乃西趨鎮州，至滹沲之中渡，與敵相遇，官軍營於滹水之南。

translations.literal: The army reached Shen Prefecture; hearing that the main Khitan force was coming, they hurried west to Zhen Prefecture; at the Zhongdu ford they met the enemy and camped south of the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: At Shenzhou they heard the main Khitan host was coming, hurried to Zhenzhou, and at Zhongdu ford met the enemy, camping south of the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敵騎潛渡至欒城，斷我糧路，尋則王清戰死，杜重威遂與守貞歸命契丹，授守貞司徒，依前鄆州節度使，從契丹至汴。

translations.literal: Before long enemy horsemen secretly crossed to Luancheng and cut the supply route; Wang Qing died in battle; Du Chongwei and Shouzhen surrendered to the Khitan; Shouzhen was made Minister of Works, remained military commissioner of Yan, and followed the Khitan to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enemy horsemen crossed to Luancheng and cut the supply road; Wang Qing was killed; Chongwei and Shouzhen surrendered to the Khitan; Shouzhen was made Minister of Works, kept Yanzhou, and followed the Khitan to Bian.

sentences.zh: 時京輦之下，契丹充斥，都人士庶，若在塗炭。

translations.literal: In the capital region the Khitan were everywhere, and the people were as if in fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital the Khitan were everywhere, and townspeople lived as if in torment.

sentences.zh: 二帥出入揚揚，市人詬之，略無慚色。

translations.literal: The two commanders went out and in proudly; people in the market cursed them with hardly a blush.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanders came and went in triumph while people in the streets cursed them without a hint of shame.

sentences.zh: 有頃，河北及京東草寇大起，澶州浮橋為群賊所斷，契丹主甚恐，乃命諸帥各歸本鎮，守貞遂赴汶陽。

translations.literal: Before long great bandit bands rose in Hebei and east of the capital; the Cang Prefecture pontoon bridge was cut; the Khitan ruler was greatly afraid and ordered each commander back to his post; Shouzhen then went to Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon great bandit bands rose in Hebei and east of the capital, the Cangzhou bridge was severed, the Khitan khan was alarmed and sent each commander back to his post; Shouzhen went to Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖入汴，守貞懼而來朝，授守貞太保，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor entered Bian, Shouzhen, fearful, came to court; he was made Grand Guardian and transferred to govern Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhiyuan entered Bian, Shouzhen, fearful, came to court, was made Grand Guardian, and was shifted to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 居無何，高祖晏駕，杜重威被誅，守貞愈不自安，乃潛畜異計。

translations.literal: Before long the High Ancestor died and Du Chongwei was executed; Shouzhen grew still more uneasy and secretly harbored divergent plans.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died and Du Chongwei was executed; Shouzhen grew still more uneasy and secretly harbored treason.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年三月，先致書於權臣，布求保證，而完城郭，繕甲兵，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Qianyou he first sent letters to powerful ministers begging guarantees, while completing his walls, repairing arms, and working day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first Qianyou year he first wrote to powerful ministers begging guarantees, while completing his walls, repairing arms, and working day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 守貞以漢室新造，嗣君才立，自謂舉無遺策，又有僧總倫者，以占術幹守貞，謂守貞有人君之位，

translations.literal: Shouzhen judged that the new Han house and the young ruler meant his plans would miss nothing; there was also the monk Zonglun, who with divination sought him out and said Shouzhen had the position of a ruler,
translations.idiomatic: He judged the young Han house easy to outwit, and a monk named Zonglun, skilled in prognostication, told him he had the markings of a ruler—

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：浚儀人趙修己，素善術數，自守貞鎮滑州，署司戶參軍，累從移鎮。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Zhao Xiuji of Junyi was skilled in numerology; since Shouzhen governed Hua Prefecture he had appointed him revenue aide and followed him through each transfer.
translations.idiomatic: (The Comprehensive Mirror: Zhao Xiuji of Junyi, skilled in numerology, had served as revenue aide since Shouzhen's days at Hua and followed him in each transfer.

sentences.zh: 為守貞言：「時命不可妄動。

translations.literal: He said to Shouzhen, "The times cannot be rashly stirred.
translations.idiomatic: He told Shouzhen, "Fate cannot be rashly stirred.

sentences.zh: 」前後切諫非一，守貞不聽，乃稱疾歸裏。）〉

translations.literal: " He counseled him repeatedly, but Shouzhen would not listen and claimed illness to return home.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He warned him again and again, but Shouzhen would not listen and pleaded illness to return home.)〉

sentences.zh: 未幾，趙思綰以京兆叛，遣使奉表送禦衣於守貞，守貞自謂天時人事合符於己，乃潛結草賊，令所在竊發，遣兵據潼關。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao Siwan rebelled at Jingzhao and sent an envoy with a memorial and imperial robes to Shouzhen; Shouzhen thought that heaven and men were aligned with him; he secretly joined with bandits to raise riots everywhere and sent troops to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao Siwan rebelled at Chang'an and sent robes and a memorial; Shouzhen thought heaven and circumstance favored him, secretly stirred bandits to rise everywhere, and sent troops to seize Tong Pass.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·王繼勛傳》：李守貞之叛，令繼勛據潼關，為郭從義所破。）〉

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Wang Jixun: In Li Shouzhen's rebellion he was ordered to hold Tong Pass and was defeated by Guo Congyi.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Song, Biography of Wang Jixun: In Li Shouzhen's revolt he was ordered to hold Tong Pass and was defeated by Guo Congyi.)〉

sentences.zh: 朝廷命白文珂、常思等領兵問罪，復遣樞密使郭威西征。

translations.literal: The court ordered Bai Wenke, Chang Si, and others to lead troops to punish him, and also sent Secretariat Director Guo Wei on a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Bai Wenke and Chang Si against him, and also dispatched Guo Wei as director of the Secretariat on a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 官軍初至，守貞以諸軍多曾隸於麾下，自謂素得軍情，坐俟扣城迎己，及軍士詬噪，大失所望。

translations.literal: When the imperial army first arrived, Shouzhen thought that many of the troops had once served under him and that he had long held their affection; he sat waiting for them to batter the gates to welcome him; when the soldiers cursed and clamored he was greatly disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army arrived he expected men who had once served under him to batter the gates to welcome him; their curses and uproar dashed his hopes.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·馬全義傳》：李守貞鎮河中，召置帳下。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Ma Quanyi: When Li Shouzhen governed Hezhong he placed Quanyi in his command.
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Song, Biography of Ma Quanyi: When Li Shouzhen held Hezhong he placed Quanyi in his command.

sentences.zh: 及守貞叛，周主討之，全義每率敢死士夜出攻周祖壘，多所殺傷。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen rebelled the Emperor of Zhou attacked; Quanyi each night led dare-to-die men to strike the Zhou camp ramparts and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: At his revolt the Zhou founder attacked; Quanyi repeatedly led death-stirrers by night against the Zhou ramparts and killed many.

sentences.zh: 守貞貪而無謀，性多忌刻，全義累為畫策，皆不能用。）〉

translations.literal: Shouzhen was greedy and without strategy, jealous by nature; Quanyi often plotted for him but none of his plans were used.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was greedy, schemeless, and jealous; Quanyi offered plans he never used.)〉

sentences.zh: 俄而王景崇據岐下，與趙思綰遣使推奉，守貞乃自號秦王，思綰、景崇皆受守貞署置。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Jingchong held the Qi foothills; together with Zhao Siwan he sent envoys to acclaim Shouzhen; Shouzhen then styled himself King of Qin, and Siwan and Jingchong all received appointments from him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Jingchong held the Qi foothills and, with Zhao Siwan, sent envoys to acclaim him; Shouzhen styled himself King of Qin, and Siwan and Jingchong accepted his commissions.

sentences.zh: 又遣人賫蠟彈於吳、蜀、契丹，以求應援。

translations.literal: He also sent wax-sealed messages to Wu, Shu, and the Khitan seeking support.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent wax-sealed messages to Wu, Shu, and the Khitan begging support.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書·朱元傳》：守貞以河中反，漢命周太祖討之，元與李平奉守貞表來乞師，未復而守貞敗。）〉

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang, Biography of Zhu Yuan: When Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong the Han sent the Zhou founder against him; Yuan and Li Ping carried Shouzhen's memorial begging for troops, but before they returned Shouzhen had fallen.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's Book of Southern Tang, Biography of Zhu Yuan: When Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong the Han sent the Zhou founder against him; Yuan and Li Ping carried Shouzhen's plea for troops, but before they returned he had fallen.)〉

sentences.zh: 既而城中糧盡，殺人為食。

translations.literal: Before long grain in the city was exhausted and they killed people for food.
translations.idiomatic: Before long grain in the city ran out and they killed people for food.

sentences.zh: 召總倫詰其休咎，總倫至曰：「王自有天分，人不能奪。

translations.literal: He summoned Zonglun to ask his fortune; when Zonglun arrived he said, "Your Highness has an allotted mandate that none can seize.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Zonglun to read his fate; Zonglun came and said, "Your Highness has heaven's portion; no man can take it.

sentences.zh: 然分野災變，俟磨滅將盡，存留一人一騎，即王鵲起之際也。

translations.literal: Yet the stars show disaster; wait until the grinding is nearly finished, with one man and one horse left—that will be the moment Your Highness rises like a magpie.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heavens show calamity; wait until the grinding is nearly finished, with one man and one horse left—that will be when you rise like a magpie.

sentences.zh: 」守貞深以為信。

translations.literal: Shouzhen deeply believed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen believed this completely.

sentences.zh: 洎攻城，守貞欲發石以拒外軍，炮竿子不可得，無何，上遊泛一筏至，其木悉可為炮竿，守貞以為神助。

translations.literal: When the siege tightened he wanted to fire stones against the outside army but could not obtain catapult poles; before long a raft floated down from upstream whose timber could all serve as poles; Shouzhen took this as divine help.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege tightened he wanted catapults but lacked poles; then a raft drifted down with timber fit for catapults, which he took as divine aid.

sentences.zh: 又嘗因宴會將佐，守貞執弧矢，遙指一虎舐掌圖曰：「我若有非常之事，當中虎舌。

translations.literal: He also once at a feast with his officers took bow and arrow and, pointing at a picture of a tiger licking its paw, said, "If I have an extraordinary affair I should strike the tiger's tongue.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast with his officers he took bow and arrow, pointed at a painting of a tiger licking its paw, and said, "If extraordinary fortune is mine, I shall strike the tiger's tongue.

sentences.zh: 」引弓一發中之，左右拜賀，守貞亦自負焉。

translations.literal: He loosed one arrow and hit it; those at left and right bowed in congratulations, and Shouzhen was also proud.
translations.idiomatic: One shot struck it; his men congratulated him and he swelled with pride.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·吳虔裕傳》：周祖討三叛，以虔裕為河中行營都監，率護聖諸軍五千以往。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Wu Qianyu: When the Zhou ancestor suppressed the three rebellions he made Qianyu superintendent of the Hezhong expeditionary camp, leading five thousand Imperial Guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: (The History of Song, Biography of Wu Qianyu: When the Zhou founder suppressed the three rebellions he made Qianyu superintendent of the Hezhong expedition with five thousand Imperial Guard troops.

sentences.zh: 李守貞出兵五千餘，設梯橋，分五路於長連城西北以禦周祖。

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen sent more than five thousand troops with scaling bridges in five columns against the northwest of the long encirclement wall to resist the Zhou ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen sent more than five thousand men with scaling bridges in five columns against the northwest of the long siege wall.

sentences.zh: 周祖令虔裕率大軍橫擊之，蒲人敗走，奪其梯橋，殺傷大半。）〉

translations.literal: The Zhou ancestor ordered Qianyu to strike horizontally; the Hezhong men fled, the bridges were taken, and more than half were killed.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder had Qianyu strike sideways; the Hezhong men fled, the bridges were taken, and more than half were killed.)〉

sentences.zh: 及周光遜以西寨降，其勢益窘，人情離散。

translations.literal: When Zhou Guangxun surrendered the western stockade the situation grew more desperate and hearts scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Guangxun surrendered the western camp the situation grew desperate and hearts scattered.

sentences.zh: 官軍攻城愈急，守貞乃潛於衙署多積薪芻，為自焚之計。

translations.literal: The imperial army pressed the siege harder; Shouzhen secretly heaped fuel in his government offices for a plan of self-immolation.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial attack grew fiercer; Shouzhen secretly heaped fodder in his yamen to burn himself.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，城陷，舉家蹈火而死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year the city fell; his whole household leapt into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year the city fell and his whole household threw themselves into the flames.

sentences.zh: 王師入城，於煙中獲其屍，斷其首函之，並獲數子二女，與其黨俱獻於闕下。

translations.literal: The imperial army entered the city, recovered his corpse from the smoke, cut off his head and cased it, and also took several sons and two daughters together with his partisans and presented them below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: The army entered, recovered his body from the smoke, cut off and boxed his head, and also took several sons and two daughters with his partisans to the capital.

sentences.zh: 隱帝御明德樓受俘馘，宣露布，百僚稱賀。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor at Mingde Tower received the captives, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and the hundred officials congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor received the captives at Mingde Tower, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and the hundred officials congratulated.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，以俘馘徇於都城，守貞首級梟於南市，諸子並賊黨孫願、劉芮、張延嗣、劉仁裕、僧總倫、靖余、張球、王廷秀、焦文傑、安在欽等並磔於西市，餘皆斬之。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished the captives were displayed in the capital; Shouzhen's head was hung at the south market; his sons and the bandits Sun Yuan, Liu Rui, Zhang Yansi, Liu Renyu, the monk Zonglun, Jing Yu, Zhang Qiu, Wang Tingxiu, Jiao Wenjie, An Zaiqin, and others were dismembered at the west market, and the rest were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites the prisoners were paraded through the capital; Shouzhen's head was hung at the south market; his sons and accomplices Sun Yuan, Liu Rui, Zhang Yansi, Liu Renyu, the monk Zonglun, Jing Yu, Zhang Qiu, Wang Tingxiu, Jiao Wenjie, An Zaiqin, and others were dismembered at the west market, and the rest were beheaded.
