translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：符後先適河中節度使李守貞之子崇訓。

translations.literal: (Omitted Text of the Five Dynasties History: Lady Fu had first married Li Shouzhen's son Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: (Omitted Text of the Five Dynasties History: Lady Fu had first married Li Shouzhen's son Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 守貞嘗得術士，善聽聲，知人貴賤，守貞舉族悉令術士聽之，獨言後大富貴，當母儀天下。

translations.literal: Shouzhen once obtained a man skilled in listening to voices who could tell noble and base rank; he had the whole clan listened to, and the man alone said she would be greatly honored and mother the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen once obtained a man who judged rank by the voice; he had the whole clan tested, and the man said only she would be greatly honored and mother the realm.

sentences.zh: 守貞信之，因曰：「吾婦尚為皇后，吾可知也。

translations.literal: Shouzhen believed this and said, "My wife would still be empress—so can I know my fate.
translations.idiomatic: Believing this he said, "My daughter-in-law would be empress—so can I know my fate.

sentences.zh: 」遂謀叛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Then he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，後獨免，周祖為世宗娶之，顯德中，冊為後。）〉

translations.literal: When the city fell she alone was spared; the Zhou founder gave her in marriage to Shizong; in the Xiande era she was enfeoffed as empress.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she alone was spared; the Zhou founder gave her in marriage to Shizong, and in the Xiande era she was enfeoffed empress.)〉

sentences.zh: 趙思綰，魏府人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Siwan, a man of Weifu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Siwan came from Weifu.

sentences.zh: 唐同光末，趙在禮之據魏城也，思綰隸於帳下，累從之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tongguang era of Tang, when Zhao Zaili held Weicheng, Siwan served in his command and followed him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Zhuangzong's Tongguang reign, when Zhao Zaili held Weicheng, Siwan served in his command and followed him through his campaigns.

sentences.zh: 在禮卒，趙延壽籍其部曲，盡付於其子贊，思綰即其首領也。

translations.literal: When Zaili died Zhao Yanshou registered his troops and gave them all to his son Zan; Siwan was their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaili died Zhao Yanshou enrolled his troops and gave them to his son Zan; Siwan was their headman.

sentences.zh: 高祖定河、洛，贊自河中移京兆尹。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor settled the He and Luo regions, Zan moved from Hezhong to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder secured the Yellow River basin, Zan moved from Hezhong to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 贊以久事契丹，常慮國家終不能容，乃與鳳翔侯益謀，引蜀兵為援，又令判官李恕入朝請覲，趙贊不待報赴闕，留思綰等數百人在京兆。

translations.literal: Zan, having long served the Khitan, feared the state would ultimately not tolerate him; with Hou Yi of Fengxiang he plotted to bring Shu troops as aid, and also sent his aide Li Shu to court to request an audience; Zhao Zan set out for court without awaiting a reply, leaving Siwan and several hundred men in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, having long served the Khitan, feared the state would never tolerate him; with Hou Yi of Fengxiang he plotted to bring in Shu troops and sent his aide Li Shu to request audience at court. Zan set out without waiting for a reply, leaving Siwan and several hundred men in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 會高祖遣王景崇等西赴鳳翔，行次京兆，時思綰等數百人在焉。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor sent Wang Jingchong west toward Fengxiang, the column passed through Jingzhao, where Siwan and his several hundred men were stationed.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder sent Wang Jingchong toward Fengxiang the column passed through Jingzhao, where Siwan and his hundreds were stationed.

sentences.zh: 思綰等比是趙在禮禦士，本不刺面，景崇、齊藏珍既至京兆，欲令文面，以防逋逸。

translations.literal: Siwan and the others had been Zhao Zaili's guard soldiers and were originally not tattooed; when Jingchong and Qi Zangzhen reached Jingzhao they wanted to tattoo their faces to prevent flight.
translations.idiomatic: These men had been Zhao Zaili's household guards and were not tattooed; Jingchong and Qi Zangzhen wanted to tattoo them at Jingzhao to prevent desertion.

sentences.zh: 景崇微露風旨，思綰厲聲先請自刺，以率其下，景崇壯之。

translations.literal: Jingchong slightly showed his intent; Siwan loudly volunteered to tattoo himself first to lead his men; Jingchong admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong hinted at the plan; Siwan loudly volunteered to tattoo himself first to lead the rest; Jingchong was impressed.

sentences.zh: 藏珍竊言曰：「思綰粗暴難制，不如殺之。

translations.literal: Zangzhen whispered, "Siwan is violent and hard to control—better kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zangzhen whispered, "Siwan is violent and hard to control—better kill him.

sentences.zh: 」景崇不聽，但率之同赴鳳翔。

translations.literal: " Jingchong would not listen but simply led them on together to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong would not listen and simply led them on to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，遣供奉官王益部署思綰等赴闕。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this it sent the attendant Wang Yi to arrange for Siwan and the others to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard, it sent the attendant Wang Yi to escort Siwan and his men to the capital.

sentences.zh: 思綰既發，行至途中，謂其黨常彥卿曰：「小太尉已入他手，吾輩至，則並死矣。

translations.literal: Once Siwan had set out, on the road he said to his follower Chang Yanqing, "The Little Governor is already in others' hands—when we reach the capital we shall die together.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were on the road he said to his follower Chang Yanqing, "The Little Governor is already in their power—when we reach the capital we shall die together.

sentences.zh: 」小太尉蓋謂趙贊也。

translations.literal: "Little Governor" meant Zhao Zan.
translations.idiomatic: "Little Governor" meant Zhao Zan.

sentences.zh: 彥卿曰：「臨機制變，子勿復言！

translations.literal: Yanqing said, "Seize the moment to change plans—say no more!
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing said, "Change course at the crisis—say no more!

sentences.zh: 」既行，至永興，副使安友規、巡檢使喬守溫出迎，於郊外離亭置酒。

translations.literal: Having set out, when they reached Yongxing the vice commissioner An Yougui and the inspector Qiao Shouwen came out to welcome them and set wine at the suburban pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On the march, at Yongxing the vice commissioner An Yougui and inspector Qiao Shouwen came out to welcome them and set wine at the suburban pavilion.

sentences.zh: 思綰前曰：「部下軍士已在城東安下，緣家屬在城，欲各將家今夜便宿城東。

translations.literal: Siwan said ahead, "My subordinates have already camped east of the city; because our families are inside the city, we wish each to bring our families out and camp east of the city tonight.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan said ahead, "My men are already encamped east of the city; because our families are inside, we want each to bring them out and camp east tonight.

sentences.zh: 」守溫等然之。

translations.literal: Shouwen and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 思綰等辭去，與部下並無兵仗，才入西門，有州校坐門側，思綰遽奪其佩劍，即斬之。

translations.literal: Siwan and his party left with their subordinates carrying no weapons; just as they entered the west gate a state sergeant sat by the gate, and Siwan suddenly snatched his sword and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan and his men left without weapons; just inside the west gate he snatched a sergeant's sword and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其眾持白挺殺守門軍士十餘人，分眾守捉諸門。

translations.literal: His followers with white clubs killed more than ten gate guards and divided forces to hold all the gates.
translations.idiomatic: His followers with white staves killed more than ten gate guards and seized the gates.

sentences.zh: 思綰劫庫兵以授之，遂據其城，時乾祐元年三月二十四日也。

translations.literal: Siwan plundered arms from the arsenal to arm them, then seized the city; that day was the twenty-fourth of the third month of the first year of Qianyou.
translations.idiomatic: He seized arms from the arsenal, armed his men, and took the city on the twenty-fourth of the third month of the first Qianyou year.

sentences.zh: 翌日，集城中丁壯得四千餘人，浚池隍，修樓櫓，旬浹之間，戰守皆備。

translations.literal: The next day he gathered more than four thousand able men in the city, deepened the moat, built towers, and within ten days had both attack and defense ready.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he gathered more than four thousand able men, deepened the moat, built towers, and within ten days had attack and defense ready.

sentences.zh: 尋遣人送款於河中，李守貞遣使賫偽詔授思綰晉昌軍節度使、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Before long he sent submission to Hezhong; Li Shouzhen sent an envoy with a forged edict appointing Siwan military commissioner of the Jinchang army and honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent submission to Hezhong; Li Shouzhen sent a forged edict making him military commissioner of Jinchang and honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，命郭從義、王峻帥師伐之。

translations.literal: When the court heard of this it ordered Guo Congyi and Wang Jun to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard, it ordered Guo Congyi and Wang Jun against him.

sentences.zh: 及攻其城，王師傷者甚眾，乃以長塹圍之。

translations.literal: In attacking the city the imperial army suffered many casualties and therefore laid a long trench encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The assault cost the imperial army dearly, so they laid a long trench around the city.

sentences.zh: 經年糧盡，遂殺人充食。

translations.literal: After a year grain was exhausted and they then killed people for food.
translations.idiomatic: After a year grain was gone and they killed people for food.

sentences.zh: 思綰嘗對眾取人膽以酒吞之，告眾曰：「吞此至一千，即膽氣無敵矣。」

translations.literal: Siwan once before the crowd took a human gall, swallowed it in wine, and told the crowd, "Swallow a thousand of these and your bold spirit will be unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan once before the crowd took a human gall, swallowed it in wine, and told them, "Swallow a thousand of these and your boldness will be matchless.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《太平廣記》：賊臣趙思綰自倡亂至敗，凡食人肝六十六，無不面剖而膾之。）〉

translations.literal: (Taiping Guangji: the rebel minister Zhao Siwan, from his rising to his defeat, ate sixty-six human livers, every one face-flayed and minced.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Taiping Guangji: the rebel Zhao Siwan, from his rising to his fall, ate sixty-six human livers, every one face-flayed and sliced.)〉

sentences.zh: 二年夏，食既盡，思綰計無從出，時左驍衛上將軍致仕李肅寓居城中，因與判官程讓能同言於思綰曰：「太尉比與國家無嫌，但負罪懼誅，遂為急計。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year, when food was exhausted, Siwan had no way out; at that time the retired Left Tiger Guard general Li Su lived in the city, and together with his administrative aide Cheng Rangneng he said to Siwan, "Grand Tutor, you lately had no quarrel with the state but only feared punishment and took desperate measures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year's summer, when food was gone, the retired Left Tiger Guard general Li Su lived in the city and, with his aide Cheng Rangneng, told Siwan, "You lately had no quarrel with the court but feared punishment and took desperate measures.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷三處用兵，一城未下，太尉若翻然效順，率先歸命，以功補過，庶幾無患。

translations.literal: The court now uses troops in three places and has not yet taken one city; if Grand Tutor turns and submits first, using merit to atone, you may escape trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The court fights on three fronts and has not taken one city—if you turn and submit first, using merit to atone, you may escape harm.

sentences.zh: 若坐守窮城，端然待斃，則何貴於智也。」

translations.literal: If you sit guarding this exhausted city and upright await death, then what worth is there in wisdom?"
translations.idiomatic: If you sit in this broken city and wait to die, what wisdom is that worth?"

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《洛陽搢紳舊聞記》：思綰主藍田副鎮，有罪已發。

translations.literal: (Old Anecdotes of Luoyang Gentry: Siwan commanded the Lantian sub-garrison; his guilt had already been exposed.
translations.idiomatic: (Old Anecdotes of Luoyang Gentry: Siwan commanded the Lantian sub-garrison; his guilt had already been exposed.

sentences.zh: 李公肅時為環衛將兼雍耀三白渠使、雍耀莊宅使、節度副使，權軍府事，護而脫之，來謝於李公。

translations.literal: Li Gongsu was then a palace guard general and concurrently commissioner of Yongyao's Sanbai Canal, commissioner of Yongyao estates, and deputy military commissioner; handling military prefecture affairs, he shielded and freed him; Siwan came to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongsu was then a palace guard general and concurrently commissioner of Yongyao's Sanbai Canal, commissioner of Yongyao estates, and deputy military commissioner; handling military prefecture affairs, he shielded and freed him; Siwan came to thank him.

sentences.zh: 公歸宅，張夫人詰之曰：「趙思綰庸賤人，公何以免其禍？

translations.literal: When he returned home Lady Zhang questioned him, "Zhao Siwan is a vulgar wretch—why did you spare him from disaster?
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home Lady Zhang questioned him, "Zhao Siwan is a vulgar wretch—why did you spare him from disaster?

sentences.zh: 又何必見之乎？

translations.literal: Why also need to see him?
translations.idiomatic: And why receive him at all?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「某比不言，夫人問，須言之。

translations.literal: " He said, "I ordinarily keep silent, but since you ask I must speak.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I ordinarily keep silent, but since you ask I must speak.

sentences.zh: 思綰者雖賤類，審觀其狀貌，真亂臣賊子，恨位下未有朕跡，不然，除去之，可也。

translations.literal: Siwan is base-born, but studying his bearing he is a true traitor who only lacks rank and an imperial record; otherwise he should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan is base-born, but studying his bearing he is a true traitor who only lacks rank and an imperial record; otherwise he should be removed.

sentences.zh: 」夫人曰：「既不能除去，何妨以小惠啖之，無使銜怨。

translations.literal: " His wife said, "Since you cannot remove him, you might as well win him with small kindness so he bears no grudge.
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "Since you cannot remove him, you might as well win him with small kindness so he bears no grudge.

sentences.zh: 」自後夫人密遣人令思綰之妻來參，夫人厚以衣物賜之，前後與錢物甚多。

translations.literal: Thereafter Lady Zhang secretly had Siwan's wife come to call; she gave her generous gifts of clothing and much money besides.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Lady Zhang secretly had Siwan's wife come to call; she gave her generous gifts of clothing and much money besides.

sentences.zh: 及漢朝，公以上將軍告老歸雍。

translations.literal: Under the Han he retired as a senior general and returned to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han he retired as a senior general and returned to Yong.

sentences.zh: 未久，思綰過雍，遂閉門據雍城叛，衣冠之族，遭塗炭者眾，公全家免禍。

translations.literal: Before long Siwan passed through Yong, shut the gates, seized the city, and rebelled; many gentry families were ruined, but Gongsu's household escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Siwan passed through Yong, shut the gates, seized the city, and rebelled; many gentry families were ruined, but Gongsu's household escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 終以計勸思綰納款，遂拔雍城。）〉

translations.literal: In the end he persuaded Siwan to submit, and the city was recovered.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In the end he persuaded Siwan to submit, and the city was recovered.)〉

sentences.zh: 思綰然之，即令讓能為章表，遣牙將劉成琦入朝。

translations.literal: Siwan agreed, had Rangneng draft the memorial, and sent his staff officer Liu Chengqi to court.
translations.idiomatic: Siwan agreed, had Rangneng draft the memorial, and sent his staff officer Liu Chengqi to court.

sentences.zh: 制授思綰華州留後、檢校太保，以常彥卿為虢州刺史，遣內臣賫官告國信賜之。

translations.literal: An edict made him acting commissioner of Hua and honorary Grand Tutor, named Chang Yanqing prefect of Guo, and sent a palace envoy with the commission and state credence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him acting commissioner of Hua and honorary Grand Tutor, named Chang Yanqing prefect of Guo, and sent a palace envoy with the commission and state credence.

sentences.zh: 既受命，遲留未發。

translations.literal: Once commissioned, he lingered and would not depart.
translations.idiomatic: Once commissioned, he lingered and would not depart.

sentences.zh: 郭從義、王峻等籌之曰：「狼子野心，終不可用，留之必貽後悔耳！

translations.literal: Guo Congyi and Wang Jun counseled, "A wolf cub keeps its wild heart—he can never be trusted; keeping him will breed regret!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi and Wang Jun counseled, "A wolf cub keeps its wild heart—he can never be trusted; keeping him will breed regret!

sentences.zh: 」既而從義、王峻等緩轡入城，陳列步騎至牙署，遣人召思綰曰：「太保登途，不暇出祖，對飲一杯，便申仳別。

translations.literal: Before long Congyi and Wang Jun entered the city at an easy pace, arrayed foot and horse at the yamen, and sent for Siwan, "Grand Tutor, you are on the road and we cannot give you a full send-off—share one cup and then part.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Congyi and Wang Jun entered the city at an easy pace, arrayed foot and horse at the yamen, and sent for Siwan, "Grand Tutor, you are on the road and we cannot give you a full send-off—share one cup and then part.

sentences.zh: 」思綰至，則執之，遂斬於市，並族其家。

translations.literal: When Siwan came they seized him and beheaded him in the market, exterminating his household as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Siwan came they seized him and beheaded him in the market, exterminating his household as well.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·郭從義傳》云：思綰困甚，從義遣人誘之，佯許以華州節鉞。

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Outline, Biography of Guo Congyi: When Siwan was desperate, Congyi sent envoys to tempt him and falsely promised the Hua commission.
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Outline, Biography of Guo Congyi: When Siwan was desperate, Congyi sent envoys to tempt him and falsely promised the Hua commission.

sentences.zh: 思綰信之，遂開門送款，從義入城，思綰謁見，即遣武士執之。）〉

translations.literal: Siwan believed him, opened the gates to submit; Congyi entered; when Siwan came to audience he was seized at once.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Siwan believed him, opened the gates to submit; Congyi entered; when Siwan came to audience he was seized at once.)〉

sentences.zh: 思綰臨刑，市人爭投瓦石以擊之，軍吏不能禁。

translations.literal: At execution the townspeople pelted him with tiles and stones; the guards could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: At execution the townspeople pelted him with tiles and stones; the guards could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 是日，並部下叛黨新授虢州刺史常彥卿等五百餘人並誅之。

translations.literal: That same day more than five hundred of his followers, including the newly appointed Guo prefect Chang Yanqing, were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day more than five hundred of his followers, including the newly appointed Guo prefect Chang Yanqing, were all executed.

sentences.zh: 籍思綰家財，得二十餘萬貫，入於官。

translations.literal: His household property was registered at more than two hundred thousand strings and taken for the state.
translations.idiomatic: His household property was registered at more than two hundred thousand strings and taken for the state.

sentences.zh: 始思綰入城，丁口僅十餘萬，及開城，惟餘萬人而已，其餓殍之數可知矣。

translations.literal: When he first took the city the population was barely one hundred thousand; when the gates opened only ten thousand remained—the toll of starvation is plain.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took the city the population was barely one hundred thousand; when the gates opened only ten thousand remained—the toll of starvation is plain.
